slides.title: Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING LLM-BASED SOCIAL SIMULATION VIA SUBJECTIVITY-ADAPTIVE SOFT-LABEL TRAINING
slides.highlight: This work introduces the subjectivity coefficient and SALT training to better model the distributional nature of human behavior in social simulations, supporting MIMIC's goal of societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: SALT improves LLM social simulations by replacing hard labels with subjectivity-adaptive soft labels to better mimic human stochasticity.
card.key_idea: Introduces a subjectivity coefficient to quantify behavioral randomness and uses it to adaptively size neighborhoods for aggregating semantically similar contexts into soft distributional labels.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new SubjSim benchmark (19,300 pairs) using Qwen3-8B; SALT significantly outperformed SFT, DPO, and PPO across KL, JSD, TVD, and MMD metrics.
card.limitation: In very low-subjectivity regimes, pooling neighbors can blur sharp targets, potentially making SALT slightly less effective than standard SFT.

slides.title: Calming Robot Pitches? Exploring the Influence of Robot Voice Pitch on Children's Stress Levels
slides.tldr: ROBOT VOICE PITCH AND CHILD STRESS
slides.highlight: This study investigates how robot voice pitch affects stress levels in children during a game, providing insights for the design of social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: Lower-pitched robot voices do not significantly reduce stress levels in children during a timed task.
card.key_idea: The study tested if manipulating a Zenbo Junior II robot's voice pitch (higher vs. lower) influenced children's self-reported stress during a challenging LEGO-building game.
card.evaluation: 27 children (ages 8-12) were evaluated using an adapted CAM-S thermometer scale. Results showed no statistically significant difference between pitch conditions.
card.limitation: Small sample size, reliance on self-report measures, and potential mismatch between the robot's cute appearance and lower-pitched voice.

slides.authors: Nina G. M. van Roij et al.

slides.title: Bayesian Partner Modelling enables Adaptive Replanning for LLM Coordination
slides.tldr: BAYESIAN PARTNER TRACKING FOR ADAPTIVE REPLANNING
slides.highlight: Introduces BayesBeliefAgent, which uses a Bayesian tracking module to infer partner skills and trigger replanning only upon contradiction. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent and adapting to evolving team goals in Overcooked environments.

card.one_liner: BayesBeliefAgent uses Bayesian partner modeling to trigger selective replanning only when teammate actions contradict beliefs.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical LLM planner paired with a Bayesian module that interrupts current skills when observed partner actions have low likelihood under the current MAP skill estimate.
card.evaluation: Tested in Overcooked/Burrito layouts against LLM and RL baselines. Metrics included reward, belief-action gap, and replan efficiency; results show significantly fewer replans.
card.limitation: The underlying LLM-based high-level skill planner remains a major performance bottleneck compared to RL-based baselines.

slides.title: Physics of Agents: Statistical Mechanics Predicts Collective Behavior of AI Agents
slides.tldr: STATISTICAL MECHANICS PREDICTS AI AGENT COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research uses a statistical-mechanics formalism to predict collective dynamics, such as polarization and consensus, in communities of language-model agents. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and the impact analysis of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Statistical mechanics predicts the collective behavior of interacting AI agents across objective and subjective questions.
card.key_idea: An Ising-model-based formalism where agents update opinions to minimize social pressure, governed by intrinsic bias and signed communication network interactions.
card.evaluation: Simulated >10,000 communities across four LLMs. Evaluated via one-step predictions and rollouts against baselines; results show superior prediction and generalization to unseen graphs.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Closing the Affective Loop: Multimodal Speaker-Listener Emotion-Dynamics-Aware Empathetic Social Robots
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL EMOTION-DYNAMICS-AWARE DIALOGUE SYSTEM
slides.highlight: This work introduces AffectLoop, a system that tracks speaker verbal and facial affective dynamics alongside the listener's state to improve embodied empathetic interaction, aligning with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: AffectLoop enables social robots to generate empathetic responses by tracking both speaker and listener affective dynamics.
card.key_idea: An LLM-based system conditioning responses on multimodal speaker dynamics (verbal VAD and facial affect) and the robot's own internal affective state to close the affective loop.
card.evaluation: Pilot within-subject study (5 participants) using Likert scales and log analysis. Results showed higher user satisfaction and stronger valence-based distress recovery than the baseline.
card.limitation: The evaluation was a small-scale pilot study with only five participants, limiting the generalizability of the results.

slides.title: Humanoid Musical Robots as Experimental Interfaces for Music-Evoked Emotion
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOTS FOR MUSIC-EVOKED EMOTION RESEARCH
slides.highlight: This work proposes using musical humanoid robots as experimental interfaces to study music-evoked emotions through controlled multimodal and embodied interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes using humanoid musical robots as controllable experimental interfaces to study music-evoked emotions.
card.key_idea: Humanoid robots enable parametric control, reproducibility, and decoupling of acoustic, visual, and interactive variables, overcoming limitations of pre-recorded auditory stimuli in music cognition research.
card.evaluation: Technical feasibility demonstrated via WAS-5 saxophonist robot, showing increased sound pressure range and successful closed-loop behavioral synchronization with human foot-tapping.
card.limitation: Constrained by current actuator/sensor technology, potential uncanny valley effects, and cultural variability in robot receptivity.

slides.authors: Vincent K. M. Cheung et al.

slides.title: Belief Without Behavior: Measuring the Translation of Theory of Mind into Coordinated Social Action in Vision-Language Models
slides.tldr: GAP BETWEEN ToM REASONING AND SOCIAL ACTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces the MOSAIC benchmark to measure how agents translate theory of mind inferences into coordinated behavior, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent and adapting for human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: VLMs struggle to translate Theory of Mind reasoning into coordinated multimodal social actions in embodied settings.
card.key_idea: MOSAIC benchmark tests agents' ability to influence others' beliefs using coordinated verbal, spatial, gaze, and facial signals across cooperative and competitive scenarios.
card.evaluation: 13 models (11 VLMs) were tested over 200 trials using TOCS, signal alignment, and sensitivity metrics; PCM-LLM was the only successful reference.
card.limitation: Evaluation is limited to a single scenario, open-source models under 15B parameters, and lacks a human performance baseline.

slides.title: HODAgent: Towards On-Demand, Responsive Humanoids for Physical World Human Interaction
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE HUMANOID SERVICE AGENT
slides.highlight: HODAgent introduces a System-2 embodied agent for humanoid robots that enables responsive task revision and interaction in service settings, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HODAgent is a System-2 embodied agent enabling responsive, on-demand human-humanoid interaction during physical task execution.
card.key_idea: A semi-duplex architecture coordinating an Env-Interactor, Planner, Executor, and hierarchical Memory to handle real-time requests, interruptions, and outcome verification across simulated and physical platforms.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a User Agent framework (164 cases) and Unitree G1 robot. Outperformed ReAct baseline in Joint Success by 9.8–18.9 percentage points.
card.limitation: Does not guarantee full-duplex or hard real-time interaction, broad cross-robot generalization, or task-level sim-to-real transfer.

slides.title: Beyond LLM-Based Reasoning: Lightweight GNNs for Agent Failure Attribution
slides.tldr: LIGHTWEIGHT GNN FOR AGENT FAILURE ATTRIBUTION
slides.highlight: Introduces AFANet, a graph-based framework for identifying faulty agents and error types in multi-agent trajectories, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and failure attribution.

card.one_liner: AFANet uses lightweight GNNs instead of heavy LLM reasoning to attribute failures in multi-agent systems.
card.key_idea: A GNN framework modeling interaction trajectories as graphs with turn-level nodes, incorporating temporal edges, intra-agent dependencies, and semantic/statistical deviation features for agent-level failure classification.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on AEGIS-Bench and Who&When datasets against various LLMs (pretrained, SFT, proprietary) using Micro/Macro-F1; AFANet matched or outperformed baselines with significantly lower cost.
card.limitation: Generalizing agent failure attribution under severe distribution shift remains an inherently challenging problem.

slides.title: X Square Robot's HOST Learns from Short Videos
slides.tldr: ROBOT LEARNS FROM SHORT VIDEOS
slides.highlight: X Square Robot's HOST demonstrates the ability to learn from short videos, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Zero-Shot Transfer of Force Map Estimation Across GelSight Mini Sensors
slides.tldr: GENERALIZABLE 3D FORCE MAP ESTIMATION
slides.highlight: This work enables the generalization of 3D force map estimation across different tactile sensor units, supporting the physics and force-based skill estimation goals of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: A two-stage method for zero-shot 3D force map estimation across different GelSight Mini sensor units.
card.key_idea: A UniT-based domain adaptation stage reconstructs tactile images into a general format, followed by a U-Net for 3D force map estimation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using SSIM (0.9338 ± 0.0358) for image reconstruction and MAE_F (1.1294 ± 1.5934N) for force estimation.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: The State of Humanoid Robotics in 2026: Trends, Challenges and Opportunities
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOTICS TRENDS 2026
slides.highlight: This analysis of humanoid robotics trends and challenges provides insights relevant to the development of embodied social robots in RwB.

slides.title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning
slides.tldr: CERTIFIED COMMUNICATION CONTROL FOR MULTI-AGENT REASONING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for orchestrating multi-agent communication through adaptive interventions and conformal calibration, contributing to HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and coordination in hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: Consilience is a framework that steers and certifies multi-agent LLM communication to solve hidden-profile reasoning tasks.
card.key_idea: It uses a state-based controller to propose communication actions, which are then validated via a round-wise conformal calibration procedure to provide finite-sample regret guarantees.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HiddenBench and a GroupTravelBench-style dataset across 12 LLMs; outperformed round-robin and sometimes full-information baselines in task accuracy.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Collective Counterfactual Planning: Coordination, Consent, and Verification under Representational Constraints
slides.tldr: FORMAL MODEL FOR COORDINATION UNDER REPRESENTATIONAL CONSTRAINTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces Collective Counterfactual Planning to model how agents with limited representational subspaces coordinate to achieve goals. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and the interaction of agent models within hybrid societies.

card.one_liner: A formal model of multi-agent planning where representational geometry, not capability, limits coordination and verification.
card.key_idea: Agents perceive and act via orthogonal projections onto subspaces. Four gates (implementation, conception, consent, and verification) determine if a team can execute and validly complete a goal.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via machine-checked numerical examples (E1, E2) and formal theorems proving the duality of collective reach and collective blindness.
card.limitation: The model is non-strategic; it assumes agents are truthful, share the goal, and consent mechanically, ignoring incentives or deception.

slides.title: When the Feature Pool Goes Algorithmic: Extending Mufwene's Ecology of Language Evolution to LLM-Mediated Exposure
slides.tldr: LLM-MEDIATED LANGUAGE EVOLUTION
slides.highlight: This work explores how LLMs act as distributional mediators that influence the frequency of linguistic variants reaching human selectors, relevant to HyECHO's focus on social perception and group norms.

card.one_liner: Proposes that LLMs act as distributional mediators that algorithmically reweight linguistic variants available to human speakers.
card.key_idea: Extends Mufwene's Ecology of Language Evolution by treating LLMs as mediators that aggregate, transform, and redistribute language, altering the frequency of variants reaching human selectors.
card.evaluation: Based on emerging evidence of model-specific linguistic profiles and lexical uptake; provides testable predictions rather than a formal empirical dataset.
card.limitation: Human social evaluation remains decisive; model-associated forms may be rejected as 'AI-like' or fail to diffuse entirely.

slides.title: Design Optimization for Large High-Force Soft Robot Manipulators Under Gravitational Loads
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING HIGH-FORCE SOFT ROBOT GEOMETRY
slides.highlight: This work introduces a method to optimize soft robot limb geometry for maximum blocking force while preventing buckling under gravity, supporting the development of large-scale robots for physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: An optimization framework for maximizing the blocking force of large soft robot limbs while preventing gravitational buckling.
card.key_idea: Uses a closed-form analytical solution based on monotonicity and convexity to optimize geometry, employing a heuristic approximation for non-uniform beams to ensure structural stability under gravity.
card.evaluation: Validated with three PneuNet prototypes; results showed maximum 6% error in buckling length prediction and confirmed the optimal design produced the highest force.
card.limitation: Requires an analytical expression for blocking force and assumes blocking force is an appropriate surrogate for general physical interaction tasks.

slides.title: Vision-Language Models for Egocentric Video: From Hand-Object Interaction to Embodied AI
slides.tldr: SURVEY OF VLMS FOR EGOCENTRIC VIDEO
slides.highlight: This survey explores how vision-language models for first-person perception support robot skill learning and human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A survey of vision-language models for egocentric video, emphasizing graph-based reasoning for embodied AI.
card.key_idea: Connects egocentric perception to embodied AI by treating relational structures (scene/hand-object graphs) as the core for modeling spatial and temporal interactions.
card.evaluation: Analyzed via benchmarks like Ego4D and EPIC-KITCHENS; notes models identify objects well but struggle with long-term action interpretation.
card.limitation: Current models fail at interpreting evolving interactions and user intent in long activities; datasets suffer from geographic and demographic biases.

slides.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE TEST-TIME COMPUTE ALLOCATION
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates a model that adaptively chooses its reasoning effort (NoThink, Short, or Long) based on problem difficulty, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt at test time.

card.one_liner: A reasoning model that adaptively selects its computation budget per problem to reduce token usage.
card.key_idea: End-to-end GRPO training where the model emits a routing token (NoThink, Short, Long) using shaped rewards, hard token caps, and a balance penalty to prevent mode collapse.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MATH-500, GSM8K, and AIME using a 1.5B distilled model; achieved 41% token reduction on MATH-500 while maintaining base accuracy.
card.limitation: Mode caps are task-specific and must be manually matched to the target task's length distribution.

slides.title: Procedural Collapse: A Structural Account of Disengagement in LLM-Assisted Writing
slides.tldr: STRUCTURAL CAUSES OF LLM DISENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: This research identifies 'procedural collapse' in AI writing interfaces, suggesting that restructuring interactions and implementing goal elicitation can support the metacognitive scaffolding necessary for ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: LLM writing tools cause 'procedural collapse' by replacing iterative writing processes with overwhelming single-output evaluations.
card.key_idea: Disengagement is structural: single-delivery interfaces compress sequential writing levels into one output, exceeding working-memory capacity and shifting the user's task from generation to costly, shallow evaluation.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper proposes a theoretical framework and design directions rather than reporting a specific empirical study.
card.limitation: The framework provides testable predictions and design directions but does not provide empirical data to validate its claims.

slides.title: Aggregating Visual Information with Optimal Transport for VideoLM Token Compression
slides.tldr: OPTIMAL TRANSPORT FOR VIDEO TOKEN COMPRESSION
slides.highlight: This work uses Optimal Transport to compress dense video token sequences into compact representations, aligning with MOSAIC's use of Optimal Transport for intent alignment and multi-view processing.

card.one_liner: AVIOT compresses VideoLM tokens by transporting dense frame observations onto a compact target measure using Optimal Transport.
card.key_idea: Casts compression as an OT problem with question-conditioned transport costs, adaptive temporal support allocation, and multi-granularity spatial fusion to preserve relevant visual information.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ten benchmarks (e.g., Video-MME, MVBench) against uncompressed baselines and CoPE; results show it matches or outperforms baselines at various compression ratios.
card.limitation: Performance gaps on LongVideoBench and LVBench may stem from limited long-video coverage in the LLaVA-Video-178K training corpus.

slides.title: TractorBeam: Personalized AI Sensemaking Support via Collaborative Machine Annotation
slides.tldr: COLLABORATIVE MACHINE ANNOTATION FOR SENSEMAKING
slides.highlight: TractorBeam uses collaborative machine annotation to provide in-context LM outputs on documents, supporting the iterative construction of mental schemas relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and state modeling.

card.one_liner: TractorBeam uses collaborative machine annotation to support exploratory sensemaking via in-context AI PDF highlighting.
card.key_idea: A browser extension where users define annotation schemas and iteratively refine LM-generated highlights using positive and negative examples directly on PDF documents.
card.evaluation: Preliminary user study with 6 domain experts using think-aloud sessions; participants reported the ability to iteratively improve model predictions.
card.limitation: Currently limited to individual documents and text; lacks support for multimodal information like tables and broader document collections.

slides.title: SleuthTalk: Supporting Historical Photo Identification with Private Workspaces for Collective Sensemaking and Deliberation
slides.tldr: COLLABORATIVE WORKSPACE FOR PHOTO IDENTIFICATION
slides.highlight: SleuthTalk provides a workspace for collective sensemaking and consensus-building in photo identification, contributing to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and group engagement.

card.one_liner: SleuthTalk provides private, structured collaborative workspaces to help researchers identify individuals in historical photographs.
card.key_idea: A system integrated into Civil War Photo Sleuth featuring custom shortlists, facial feature annotation, threaded discussions, and consensus-building polls for trusted small-group deliberation.
card.evaluation: Mixed-methods study with six experienced researchers comparing SleuthTalk to Facebook; analyzed via system logs and semi-structured interviews.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.
